issues.title: Non-strict off-diagonal support boundary

failure_location.quote: $Z_{ik}\in\mathbb{C}^{n_i^{(j)}\times n_k^{(j)}}$ is a matrix that the $(s,t)$-element of $Z_{ik}$ is zero if $s+t\geq\max\{n_i^{(j)}, n_k^{(j)}\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that every off-diagonal entry with s+t at least max{n_i,n_k} is zero. In exa1, n_i=3 and n_k=2, while the displayed admissible form retains f_{12} at (1,2) and f_{21} at (2,1), both on the equality boundary s+t=3. Thus the old condition excludes entries allowed by the defining equation and the paper's own example; replacing the relation by a strict inequality removes that erroneous boundary exclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The old prose gives an overly restrictive support description for off-diagonal blocks in Theta, but no later formal result relies on that particular non-strict boundary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the off-diagonal support condition by: the (s,t)-entry of Z_{ik} is zero when s+t>max{n_i^{(j)},n_k^{(j)}}. Equality-boundary entries remain permitted, and no downstream statement requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: Equation gs-19 and exa1 uniquely force the strict boundary: the displayed equality-boundary entries are valid. This is a transcriptional comparison error that an intended reader can correct without repairing an argument or construction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: the $(s,t)$-element of $Z_{ik}$ is zero if $s+t>\max\{n_i^{(j)}, n_k^{(j)}\}$.

issues.title: Off-by-one terminal block in the simple-spectrum parameterization
issues.failure_explanation: The old block inventory permits ordinary paired blocks only through index r-2. The T-palindromic formula nevertheless includes xi_{r-1}, and the T-anti-palindromic formula similarly includes hat xi_{r-1} in addition to its exceptional scalar blocks. Thus the displayed parameter matrix has one excess 2-by-2 block and is incompatible with its declared 2n-by-2n size.
issues.overall_effect: The T-case characterization in cor-1 is dimensionally wrong, and thm-IEP's reference to a parameter matrix of that form is consequently malformed for those cases.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In both T-cases of cor-1, terminate the ordinary paired-block sequence at index r-2 rather than r-1; retain the exceptional scalar blocks a and b in the T-anti-palindromic case. Read thm-IEP's reference to cor-1 using this corrected 2n-by-2n inventory.
issues.why_classification: The earlier block range ends at r-2, and the stated dimension identity uniquely rules out the additional block. Correcting the copied terminal index restores cor-1 and its use in thm-IEP without changing any mathematical inference or guarantee.

issues.title: Extra square root in the semisimple normalizer
issues.failure_explanation: The blockwise calculation defines D_{jj}=diag(D_j,D_j)^{1/2} and establishes normalization by D_{jj}^{-1} on both sides. The old global definition instead takes diag(D_{11},...,D_{r-2,r-2})^{1/2}, producing fourth-root rather than square-root scaling. Consequently the claimed identity gs-34 does not follow unless all singular values happen to equal one.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm-s-1 fails to construct the claimed canonical parameter matrix, although the theorem is recovered by the locally forced definition of D.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define D=diag(D_{11},D_{22},...,D_{r-2,r-2}), retaining D_{jj}=diag(D_j,D_j)^{1/2}, and use this corrected D throughout the normalization and transformed-standard-pair calculation.
issues.why_classification: With the printed extra square root, D has fourth-root scaling and the asserted identity gs-34 is false, so the proof construction genuinely requires repair rather than mere reading correction. The blockwise calculation already forces the corrected definition, and a short routine verification then recovers thm-s-1 with no loss of scope or conclusion.

issues.title: General-sign PQIEP invocation exceeds the printed theorem

failure_location.quote: Thus, if the matrix $X\Lambda\Gamma X^{\star}$ with $X=YP$ is nonsingular, then we can get a solution of PQIEP by Theorem \ref{thm-IEP}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the preceding epsilon-dependent construction, including the anti-palindromic cases, produces a PQIEP solution by thm-IEP. The old formal Problem instead asks for a (star,1)-palindromic polynomial, and thm-IEP concludes only Q-star=Q with the +A-star residual. Thus the cited theorem does not support the claimed epsilon=-1 applicability, even though the earlier main-thm contains the sign-aware framework.
issues.overall_effect: The printed application overstates the scope of the cited inverse-eigenvalue theorem: its palindromic cases are covered, but its anti-palindromic conclusion is not certified by thm-IEP as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the PQIEP and thm-IEP consistently for general epsilon: request a (star,epsilon)-palindromic polynomial, use the residual AXΛ²+QXΛ+epsilon A-star X=0, and conclude Q-star=epsilon Q. Then obtain thm-IEP directly from main-thm with J=Λ, validating the final invocation for both signs.
issues.why_classification: The printed Problem and thm-IEP coherently cover only epsilon=1, so their use for the anti-palindromic cases is not a typo. However, main-thm already supplies exactly the sign-aware result, making the complete repair a short local specialization with no new lemma, proof architecture, or mathematical loss.
